 Govt forms new wage board for garment sector 
 Published : 1 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 1 November 2026, 12:17
 • 
 NEWS
 SHARE 
 BSS, Dhaka 
 The government has constituted a wage board to review the minimum wage structure for garment workers, comprising representatives from employers, workers, and neutral parties to determine the minimum wage for garments workers. 
 The Ministry of Labour and Employment issued two separate notifications in this regard today.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 Read more Police vehicle set on fire as RMG workers, police clash in Mirpur 
 According to a notification, ABM Shamsuddin, a director of Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), has been appointed as the representative for the employers, while Babul Akhter, general secretary of Bangladesh Garment and Industrial Workers Federation, as the representative for the workers.
 In another notification, Dr Mosleh Uddin Ahmad, a professor of the Department of Public Administration at Dhaka University, has been appointed as a neutral member, while Asif Ayub, joint secretary-general of the Bangladesh Employers Federation, as an employers' representative and Anwar Hossain, president of Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal, as a workers' representative.
 These appointments have been made in line with Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 (as amended in 2026).
 Read more Production halted at three RMG factories in Ashulia over wage demands 
 The notifications have asked the chairman of the minimum wage board to initiate the necessary proceedings - in consultation with the representatives of the employers, workers, and the neutral members - to determine the minimum wage for garment workers.
